_mode: audit-only (no code modified, no fetch calls)

comic_claims_c_slug_page.post_signin_resume: localStorage 'pending_claim_slug' + window focus listener retries claim
comic_claims_c_slug_page.verification_step: implicit — backend trusts signed-in user owns the claimed slug. NO evidence (no Instagram URL, photo, ID) collected on frontend.
comic_claims_c_slug_page.ux_outcome_success: banner turns green + links to /c/<slug>.html; data refreshes on next daily build

show_runner_claims_show_page.evidence_in_repo: shows/south-comedy-club.html line 98 (+ all other generated show pages)
show_runner_claims_show_page.handler: book.html submitShowRunner() BLOCK 2 lines 487-524 — claim branch checks URLSearchParams.get('claim')
show_runner_claims_show_page.submission: POST /api/show/claim {show_slug, show_name, source_url, venue, claimant_name, claimant_email, role:'show_runner', message:'day=...,time=...,eventbrite=...'}
show_runner_claims_show_page.verification_step: out-of-band — frontend success msg promises 'we review every claim within 48 hours before any ownership badge is shown publicly'
show_runner_claims_show_page.evidence_collection: Eventbrite URL field is optional and goes into the `message` field as a freeform string. No Instagram, photo, venue confirmation, or domain-bound email check.
show_runner_claims_show_page.ownership_badge: shows/<slug>.html calls /api/show/<slug>/ownership → '✓ Managed by show runner' | '◯ Unclaimed show page'
show_runner_claims_show_page.post_claim_portal: show-runner.html (separate token-based portal — owner_token via magic link, NOT linked to the book.html claim form)

booker_account_activation.auth_required: email magic link (booker_token; dev mode reveals dev_token inline)
booker_account_activation.verification_step: payment reconciliation — booker_portal.html step 2: 'The operator reconciles payment. The admin endpoint marks the payment paid and activates the Booker Plus account.' — purely manual
booker_account_activation.booker_claims_a_show: NOT a separate flow — bookers use /booker-dashboard.html to CREATE shows (POST /api/booker/shows). There is no 'claim an existing show as a booker' UI distinct from the show-runner claim. A booker who wants to take an existing pariscomedy.com show goes through the same book.html?claim=<slug> path with role='show_runner'.

venue_claim.detail: data/schema.json mentions venues.claimed + venues.claimed_by_user_id, but no UI in /venues.html, /v/*.html or anywhere else exposes a claim CTA for venues.

verification_step_summary.comic: magic-link email → backend trusts user-controls-email-of-record. No second factor.
verification_step_summary.show_runner: manual 48h admin review (advertised in success msg) — actual review queue not present in repo (see P3.SUBMIT.1).
verification_step_summary.booker: manual payment reconciliation by admin (no automated link between paid invoice and claim).

evidence_collection.instagram_url: NOT collected on any claim form
evidence_collection.photo_or_id: NOT collected on any claim form
evidence_collection.domain_bound_email: NOT enforced (e.g., booker can claim with @gmail.com even if show is at venue.fr)
evidence_collection.freeform_proof_text: book.html claim payload's `message` field is the only place a claimant can leave context; not surfaced in any admin UI in the repo

broken_or_missing_handlers.detail: Claim submission has no evidence step (no Instagram, no photo, no domain-bound email). 48h admin review is unsourced — admin has only claimant name + email + day/time/eventbrite freeform message to verify ownership.

POST /api/performer/claim only sends {slug}. Backend (not in this repo) has no signal that the signed-in user IS that comic beyond claimant assertion. A bad actor with a verified email can claim any comic slug.
No 'pending claim' visibility on the public page or to other potential owners. If two people claim the same slug, neither sees the conflict on the frontend.

/shows/<slug>.html line 123 links 'Report it' → /book.html?report=<slug> but book.html does NOT handle ?report= (no preloadReport function, only preloadClaim). The Report link is decorative and lands users on the show-runner submit form with no context.
Schema defines venues.claimed / claimed_by_user_id, but no UI exists for a venue to claim its page. Dead schema field.

claimant-name-field is display:none and only revealed when ?claim=<slug> is present. If preloadClaim IIFE fails (e.g. claim slug param empty after URL rewrite), the user submits an unclaimed show listing with no claimant_name and the JS error path leaves the form in a confusing state.
Response field `dev_token` is echoed into the input + UI message. If the production API ever returns it (debug flag stuck on), it's leaked into the DOM.

On /api/show/<slug>/ownership fetch failure, badge silently renders '◯ Unclaimed show page'. A backend outage looks identical to 'never claimed' to the public — claimants lose their verified badge during downtime.

slug.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9-]/g, '') silently strips characters. Slugs with uppercase or unicode (none currently, but possible from URL share) are mutated without warning, leading to claims for the wrong/non-existent slug.
localStorage 'pending_claim_slug' persists indefinitely. window focus triggers re-submit; stale slugs from old tabs can re-fire claims days/weeks later.
Venue field is prefilled from URL param but NOT readonly. Claimant can edit the venue, contradicting the show being claimed. show_name is locked; venue is not — inconsistent.

Banner innerHTML interpolates slug directly: `Claiming "${slug}"`. Sanitizer at line 190 strips most chars, but slug still flows into innerHTML rather than textContent. Safe today (filter removes <>), but fragile against future filter relaxation.

Show-runner uses 'Bearer <owner_token>' header + GET ?owner_token=. Performer-portal uses cookie session (credentials:'include'). Booker-portal uses 'X-Booker-Token' header. Three different auth schemes for three portals — high cognitive cost + harder to audit.

summary.primary_finding: All 3 claim flows (comic / show-runner / booker) lack evidence collection. Authority is delegated to backend admin review with effectively no proof on the frontend. /shows/*.html ?report= links are dead. Venue-claim schema exists but has no UI.

P3.CLAIM.3 — Add evidence-collection fields to show-runner claim (Instagram of show, last poster URL, domain-bound email if venue has a domain).
P3.CLAIM.5 — Unify auth across 3 portals (one session model, one helper).
P3.CLAIM.6 — Add venue-claim UI on /venues.html and /v/<slug>.html OR remove the schema field.
P3.CLAIM.7 — Expire localStorage 'pending_claim_slug' after N hours; require explicit re-click after refresh.
P3.CLAIM.8 — Fix ownership badge fail-open: distinguish 'unclaimed' from 'ownership API offline'.
P3.CLAIM.9 — Lock the venue field in claim mode (parity with show_name).
